day_03_morning: ^The stair below the foundry goes down farther than the maps admit.
^Mara counts the steps. Iven counts the exits. You count the times you have done this before.
^The counterweights are still moving. That is the first bad sign.
^They should have stopped when the Bell cracked.
^The second bad sign is the singing.
^It comes up through the floor, low and patient, a hymn with no words.
^Iven stops at the lock mechanism. Give me ten minutes, he says. I can slow the drop.
^Ten minutes is a long time in a burning building.
trust: ^Iven opens the panel. His hands are steady. They are always steady when there is something to fix.
^Mara watches the dark below. You watch Iven.
^Nine minutes, he says. Then we run.
lead: ^You go first. The stair groans under each step.
^Mara follows close enough that you can hear her breathing.
^If the floor goes, Iven says from behind, I am blaming you.
day_03_afternoon: ^The counterweight hall is a cathedral built for machines. Chains hang from the dark like roots.
^At the bottom, the Ashwright is waiting. It has rebuilt itself from the foundry's bones.
^The Hollow Choir circles above it, a ring of notes with no mouths.
^You came back, the Ashwright says. Good. The Bell needs a witness.
^The main chain is exposed. If it goes, the whole hall comes down.
cut: ^Mara swings. The chain opens with a sound like a bell being born.
^The Ashwright turns, too late, and the hall begins to fall.
face: ^You step into the ring. The Choir tightens around you like a noose of sound.
^The Ashwright lifts its hammer. The Bell in your chest answers.
^This time, you say, I am not here to watch.
day_03_night: ^The Choir finds you on the Spire stair. It does not attack. It offers.
^Give us the loop, it sings. Give us the ninth day. We will make the Bell whole.
^Mara's hand is on her hammer. Iven's hand is on his arbalest. Neither of them moves.
^No one will remember, the Choir says. No one will have to.
^The crack in the Bell glows faintly. It is waiting for an answer.
^Listen. Ask what the city would lose.
refuse: ^No, you say. The word is small. The Bell takes it anyway.
^The Choir withdraws like a tide. Mara exhales.
^That was the right answer, she says. I think.
listen: ^Everything that hurts, the Choir says. And everything that made the hurting bearable.
^You listen until the song ends. Then you tell it to leave.
bargain: ^Take the foundry, you say. Take every debt in Ember Row. Leave the people.
^The Choir considers this. It is not mercy, it says. It is arithmetic.
